courseContributions.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: Financial statements, double-entry, costs and investment appraisal support the accounting/business setting. No tax-base computation, Dutch fiscal accounting or corporation-tax doctrine inferred.

courseContributions.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: AI business and policy is a possible context of regulation; too indirect to define a tax-law response.

courseContributions.name: Transnational Business Law
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: Comparative transnational commercial contracts, trade, investment and disputes; actual advice/arbitration/oral advocacy develops legal application. No specialist corporate-tax rules inferred.

courseContributions.name: Money, Banking & Finance
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: Financial markets, bonds, derivatives, banks, interest rates and central-bank policy support business-finance context; not a tax-law substitute.

courseContributions.name: Introduction to Economics
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: Introductory micro/macro principles supply economic preparation; do not replace legal taxation study.

courseContributions.name: International Macroeconomics
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: International macroeconomics supplies cross-border economic context, not double-tax treaty or tax-residence doctrine.

courseContributions.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: Microeconomics, welfare, market failure and externalities support behavioural/public-policy reasoning about taxation.

courseContributions.name: Public Economics
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: Public Economics directly addresses taxation/incidence, equity/efficiency, public goods/expenditure and redistribution through models and a policy research paper. Strong fiscal-policy contribution, not fiscal legislation/case law.

courseContributions.name: Econometrics
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: Econometrics description supports estimation(OLS/GLS/IV), tests and research/Monte-Carlo work for empirical policy analysis. Fully considered without enhanced profile; no tax-specific study assumed.

courseContributions.name: Behavioral Economics
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: Behavioural Economics description supports biases, framing and experimental methods relevant to incentive responses. Fully considered; no tax-enforcement doctrine assumed.

courseContributions.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: Rights, legal/philosophical sources, treaties and case analysis support legal reasoning and fairness questions; not fiscal procedure.

courseContributions.name: Criminal Law & Criminal Justice
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: Criminal liability, legal-advice clinic, written/oral argument and criminology research can support enforcement analysis. No tax offences or financial-investigation specialism inferred.

courseContributions.name: Introduction to Public International Law
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: Public international law sources/treaties/judgments and research build international legal method; not international tax-treaty specialisation.

courseContributions.name: Comparative Constitutional Law
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: Comparative constitutional/administrative institutions, remedies and procedural fairness are substantively relevant to taxpayer-government relationships; no detailed Dutch assessment/objection rules inferred.

courseContributions.name: Principles of Private Law
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: Comparative private property, tort and contract law with IRAC/case briefs/mediation research supports legal foundations and commercial relationships; not fiscal company law.

courseContributions.name: Foundations of European Union Law
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: EU institutions, supremacy, remedies and free-movement case law support European legal context; no guarantee of harmonised tax-law coverage.

courseContributions.name: Ethics
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: Ethical reasoning/texts and independent argument support fairness and distributive evaluation; no statutory fiscal competence inferred.

courseContributions.name: Public Policy Analysis
courseContributions.contributionAndLimit: Public Policy Analysis description supports policy analysis/memos and a sugar-policy context. Fully considered without an enhanced profile; not a fiscal-law sequence.
